t: That section 4 of the Act entitled “An Act to control the possession, sale, transfer, and use of pistols and other dangerous weapons in the District of Columbia, to provide penalties, to prescribe rules of evidence, and for other purposes”, approved July 8, 1932 (sec. 22, 3204 D. C. Code, 1940 edition), be amended by changing the last period to a colon and adding the following language: “Provided, That arrests, without a warrant, and searches and seizures pursuant thereto, may be made for violation of this section, by police officers, as in the case of a felony, upon probable cause that the person arrested is violating this section at the time of the arrest; but no evidence discovered in the course of any arrest, search, or seizure authorized by this proviso shall be admissible in any criminal proceeding against the person arrested unless at the time of such arrest he was carrying a pistol or other dangerous weapon on or about his person.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to a "criminal proceeding" and to arrests of persons involve outside parties interacting with the government. That fails because the section only authorizes warrantless arrests by police for weapons violations in the District of Columbia and sets an evidence-admissibility rule. It provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right for an outside party to sue over a federal decision.
fable.s: arrests, without a warrant, and searches and seizures pursuant thereto, may be made for violation of this section, by police officers, as in the case of a felony, upon probable cause that the person arrested is violating this section at the time of the arrest

qwen_block.w: This section defines the legal standards for warrantless arrests and the admissibility of evidence in criminal proceedings. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) in a federal decision-making process. The actors involved are police officers and courts, which are part of the government or judicial system, not outside participants influencing a policy decision.
qwen_block.s: Provided, That arrests, without a warrant, and searches and seizures pursuant thereto, may be made for violation of this section, by police officers, as in the case of a felony, upon probable cause that the person arrested is violating this section at the time of the arrest; but no evidence discovered in the course of any arrest, search, or seizure authorized by this proviso shall be admissible in any criminal proceeding against the person arrested unless at the time of such arrest he was carrying a pistol or other dangerous weapon on or about his person.

opus.w: This amendment to the D.C. weapons law lets police arrest without a warrant and limits when evidence from those arrests can be used. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or consultation with outsiders, and it gives no one a right to sue over a government decision. The reference to a criminal proceeding concerns the rules of evidence in a prosecution, not outside input into a policy decision.
opus.s: no evidence discovered in the course of any arrest, search, or seizure authorized by this proviso shall be admissible in any criminal proceeding against the person arrested

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes rules of evidence for criminal proceedings, specifically regarding the admissibility of evidence obtained during warrantless arrests. It does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The definition excludes litigation procedures and court jurisdiction from the scope of 'participation'.
qwen_chat.s: no evidence discovered in the course of any arrest, search, or seizure authorized by this proviso shall be admissible in any criminal proceeding against the person arrested unless at the time of such arrest he was carrying a pistol or other dangerous weapon on or about his person
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the mention of "arrests" and "criminal proceedings" implies a right to participate in the legal process (e.g., via a hearing or trial). However, the definition explicitly excludes "a court's jurisdiction, venue, or the statute-of-limitations period for suits" and focuses on consultation/coordination *before* a federal decision. This text defines the conditions for admissibility of evidence in court, which is a procedural rule for litigation, not a mechanism for outside parties to consult with the government before a decision is made. The actors involved are police officers (federal/local law enforcement) and the accused, but the interaction is adversarial litigation, not participatory decision-making.
